items.details: 1a: data/lint-rules.json template-leftover is now \{\{[^{}\n]{0,80}\}\} and open-placeholder \[\[[^\[\]\n]{1,120}\]\] (no test showed a need to adjust); the other 5 rules were checked and are linear (slowest adversarial input 0.8-6.9 ms at 50k chars). The $comment documents the linear-time rule. 1b: mcp/src/check.ts collapses every whitespace run to one space, matches per line, and matches long lines in overlapping windows (2,000 chars, 300 overlap; one lead char so \b and ^ stay correct, each match reported once) instead of truncating, so text past 2,000 chars is still checked. All own signals use bounded repetition only (number pattern \b\d[\d,]{0,15}\s{0,3}..., [\w-]{1,40}, [\w'-]{1,30}, \d{1,4}, \s?). Signals are combined into one alternation per area and target kind (fewer exec calls). For 'regardless of the data file': new isBoundedPattern() gate; rules with *, +, {n,}, {n,m} above 200 or after a group, or backreferences are skipped (SKIPPED_LINT_RULES; the summary says so, and an mcp test asserts none are skipped). 1c: kept PROMPT_MAX_CHARS = 100,000: warm tools/call check_prompt <= 61 ms for every adversarial shape; worst checkPrompt cold ~88 ms; first request of a fresh process for 50k one-letter lines 145-169 ms in three runs, of which ~50-65 ms is the server's own first-request start-up. 1d: 16 adversarial timing cases at 100k chars (text and Midjourney targets) in mcp/test/check.test.ts, bound 500 ms. 1e: scripts/test/lint-rules.test.mjs (zero-dependency node:test) builds 78-413 adversarial 50,000-char inputs per rule from the pattern's own literals and class characters, runs each under a vm timeout (2 s) so a catastrophic pattern fails rather than hangs, bound 500 ms; a control test proves it catches both old patterns (both time out). CONTRIBUTING.md documents the rule.
items.tests: mcp/test/check.test.ts: 'time on adversarial input' (16 cases), isBoundedPattern accept/reject cases, SKIPPED_LINT_RULES empty, long-line window tests (match past 2,000 chars, edge-crossing match counted once at 11 shifts, no mid-line heading). scripts/test/lint-rules.test.mjs: 7 rule tests + validity + control. Reintroducing the old template pattern or the old \d[\d,]* signal in a scratch copy makes these fail.

items.details: 2a: check_prompt description, INSTRUCTIONS and the report header say the checks match English keywords and headings only. 2b: looksMostlyEnglish(): mostly non-Latin letters means non-English; else, with 12+ words, an English function-word share under 5% plus other-language function words (8%+) or accented words (15%+). Correct on 8 English samples (incl. terse image prompts and SD tag lists) and 18 other languages. Unmatched areas then report status 'unknown' (text: 'unknown (keyword checks are English-only)'); found areas stay found (e.g. --ar in a German Midjourney prompt); lint still runs. Schema change: dimensions[].present replaced by status ('found' | 'not found' | 'unknown'), plus top-level mostlyEnglish. 2c: brief step 4 says 'consider what it flags', and INSTRUCTIONS step 5 too. 2d: format words (json/yaml/csv/xml/markdown/html, schema) count only in output phrases ('as/in/into JSON', 'return/respond ... JSON', 'JSON object/array/output/response/schema', 'output/response schema'), so 'build a JSON parser in rust' and 'Design a database schema' no longer count as Output format.

notes: Nothing committed, pushed or reset. During my work the orchestrator committed d63abbf (universal prompt change); my regenerated content.ts includes it, and build --check is clean. Deviations and trade-offs to review: (1) Long lines are matched in overlapping 2,000-char windows rather than truncated, so no content is skipped; in addition check_prompt refuses data rules with unbounded or repeated-group repetition (isBoundedPattern), which is what makes it linear whatever the data file holds. (2) The decided template-leftover pattern also flags JSX double braces such as style={{ margin: 0 }} in coding prompts, which the old pattern didn't. (3) Bracketed text longer than 120 chars is no longer reported as an open placeholder, which is why excerpt.mjs now reports no finding. (4) Schema changes: check_prompt dimensions[].present became status ('found'|'not found'|'unknown') plus top-level mostlyEnglish; ask_user status no longer has 'cancelled'; why is required; new notes_label and notes_hint inputs. (5) Unreadable stdio lines that aren't JSON are silently dropped by the SDK (not logged); valid JSON that isn't JSON-RPC logs 'ignored a message that is not valid JSON-RPC (invalid-message)'; a malformed HTTP body isn't logged at all. (6) Item 13 is partial: mcpb 2.1.2 always prints the 512x512 'recommendation' for a valid PNG. Scratch artifacts (timing scripts, mutation script, patched probe copies) are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-prompt-engine/d32a46dc-34ea-5901-8086-72e22db65686/scratchpad/fix/; the scratch repo copy used for mutation tests was deleted.

Own end-to-end tools/call check_prompt timings at 100k chars through createMcpHandler, each case in a fresh process: first request 65-84 ms for single-line shapes and 145-169 ms over three runs for 50,000 one-letter lines; of that, 50-65 ms is the server's own first-request start-up (a fresh process's first tools/list takes about 51 ms). Later calls: 6-23 ms single-line, 31-61 ms many lines. Node 20.20.2 checkPrompt worst: 57.6 ms (single-line suite), 81.4 ms (many lines). Lint-rule harness at 50k chars: pressure-words 3.6 ms, visible-reasoning-request 2.0, magic-phrase 2.7, prefill-instruction 6.9, template-leftover 1.9, open-placeholder 0.8, vague-quality-words 3.1; both old patterns hit the 1 s timeout.
